item.text: I’m reviewing the current structure first. The next useful pass should target repetition and API friction in the newer abstractions, not the matrix-chain algorithm itself.

I found a cleaner API boundary: `MatrixDimensions` is already the real domain type, but it’s still hidden as an internal helper. I’m making that type first-class and tightening the solver around it so callers can reuse validated dimensions without array copying on every call.
I’ve promoted the dimensions type into the public API. Next I’m updating the facade and solver to use that API directly and to cache the size internally instead of re-reading it through the loops.
The API cleanup is in. I’m compiling and running both the library-facing and CLI-facing paths now to make sure the public type promotion didn’t change behavior.

Refactored the API around `MatrixDimensions`, which is now a first-class public value type instead of an internal helper. [MatrixDimensions.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixDimensions.java:3) now owns validation, parsing, defensive copying, and indexed access through a clearer public surface (`of`, `parse`, `size`, `valueAt`). [MatrixChainMultiplication.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixChainMultiplication.java:14) now exposes a `solve(MatrixDimensions)` overload, so callers can reuse validated dimensions directly instead of re-wrapping raw arrays on every call.

I also tightened [MatrixChainSolver.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/019_matrix_chain_multiplication/MatrixChainSolver.java:16) by caching `dimensionCount` in the solver state and switching internal access from the old helper names to the new value-object API. That removes repeated size lookups and makes the DP code read against the domain type rather than a loose array wrapper.

Verified with `javac MatrixChainMultiplication.java MatrixChainSolver.java MatrixChainResult.java MatrixDimensions.java MatrixChainCli.java`, `java -cp . MatrixChainCli`, and `java -cp . MatrixChainCli 2 1 3 4`; both runs still printed `20`.
